description:
Château du Nessay was built in the late 19th century on the ruins of a medieval fortress, at the tip of a peninsula in the harbor of Saint-Briac-sur-Mer. It stood abandoned for a long time, becoming a gathering place for generations of children who visited the castle. Le Nessay was born from a desire to completely rehabilitate this "sleeping beauty." It opened as a hotel in 2018 and is today a member of Small Luxury Hotels of the World.

Today its 17 rooms are split three ways: 11 within the château itself, 4 in the building's historic posterns, and 2 in a separate annex facing the château, on the beach — all with sea or beach views.

The site's medieval fortress origins, visible only as ruins beneath the current late-19th-century building, give Nessay a documented history stretching back centuries before the structure guests see today.

The château's long abandonment and informal role as a childhood gathering place, before its deliberate 2018 rehabilitation, gives the property a specific local memory distinct from estates that passed continuously through noble or commercial ownership.

The presence of a genuine, separate beachfront annex — 2 of the 17 rooms — distinguishes Nessay from château-hotels where all rooms sit within a single historic footprint, even though the large majority of rooms here remain within the château and its posterns.

The château's position on Brittany's Emerald Coast, near Dinard and Saint-Malo, gives guests staying at Nessay easy access to two of the region's best-known coastal towns.
history: Château du Nessay was built in the late 19th century on the ruins of a medieval fortress, at the tip of a peninsula in Saint-Briac-sur-Mer's harbor. Long abandoned, it became a gathering place for local children before being fully rehabilitated and opened as a hotel in 2018; it is now a member of Small Luxury Hotels of the World. Its 17 rooms are split between the château (11), its historic posterns (4), and a separate beachfront annex (2).

faqs.question: Are all the rooms at Château du Nessay within the château building?
faqs.answer: Most are — 11 of the 17 rooms are within the château itself and 4 more in its historic posterns, but 2 rooms are in a separate annex facing the château, on the beach.

faqs.question: What stood on this site before the current château?
faqs.answer: A medieval fortress, whose ruins the late-19th-century château was built upon.

faqs.question: When did Château du Nessay open as a hotel?
faqs.answer: In 2018, after a full rehabilitation; it is now a member of Small Luxury Hotels of the World.

hotel.how_to_stay:
**Getting there:** On Brittany's Emerald Coast, near Dinard and Saint-Malo.

**Rooms & rates:** 17 rooms, most within the 19th-century château (including its historic posterns), with 2 in a separate beachfront annex facing the building; from about €318 per night.

**On-site:** Spa, restaurant, direct beach access.

**Good to know:** Built on the ruins of a medieval fortress, the current building dates to the late 19th century — most rooms are in the château and its historic posterns, but 2 of the 17 are in a separate beachfront annex.

**Combine with:** Saint-Malo (20 min), Dinard (15 min).
